draft.title: Black body radiation
card: A black body is an ideal object that absorbs all radiation that hits it. When hot, it gives off a continuous spectrum of radiation that depends only on its temperature.
Wien's law says the peak wavelength is inversely proportional to the temperature in kelvin: λmax = b ÷ T. The constant b is about 2.9 × 10^-3 m K.
So as an object gets hotter, the peak moves to a shorter wavelength, and the object gives off more energy overall. A cooler object peaks at a longer wavelength.
Classical physics could not explain the shape of the spectrum. Planck fixed this by assuming energy is given off in separate packets, not in a smooth flow.
draft.remember: Hotter means a shorter peak wavelength. Planck explained the spectrum with energy in packets.

a.q: A metal bar is heated in a furnace and its temperature rises. What happens to the peak wavelength of the radiation it gives off?
opts: It becomes longer, but the energy given off falls
a.why: Wien's law says peak wavelength is inversely proportional to temperature, so a hotter bar peaks at a shorter wavelength. It is tempting to think the wavelength grows with the heat, but that reverses the relationship.
a.clue: Wien's law links peak wavelength and temperature inversely.

b.q: Star X has a surface temperature of 6000 K. Star Y has a surface temperature of 3000 K. Both act as black bodies. How do their peak wavelengths compare?
opts: Star X's is half of Star Y's
Star X's is double Star Y's
Star X's is the same as Star Y's
Star X's is a quarter of Star Y's
b.why: Peak wavelength is inversely proportional to temperature in kelvin. Star X is twice as hot, so its peak wavelength is half that of Star Y. Doubling the temperature does not double the wavelength, because the relationship is inverse.
b.clue: Inversely proportional means doubling one halves the other.

b.best: Star X's is half of Star Y's

problems.detail: The clue 'Inversely proportional means doubling one halves the other' all but gives the answer. The temperatures are plainly doubled (6000 K vs 3000 K), so the student only has to apply 'halves' without reasoning.

The clue states the inverse link between peak wavelength and temperature, which is exactly what the question tests. Once told 'inversely', a rising temperature leads straight to 'shorter', so the clue largely gives the answer away.
